newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks lower in depressed demand.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks lower in depressed demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares on Tuesday were depressed in minimal demand as local funds refrained from buying in the absence of substantial foreign purchases, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.12 percent to 166.46 points in minimal 431,739 dinar turnover ($608,940).
The busiest traded stock, Jordan Cement Factories was unchanged at 3.99 dinars in 86,092 dinars worth of trade rumoured to have been mainly foreign-inspired.

Among the few stocks which witnessed some demand was Jordan Islamic Bank and El Zay garments manufacturer. The first was unchanged at 3.91 dinars and the latter rose 0.07 dinars to 1.51 dinars in trade worth 9,330 dinars.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, rose 0.07 percent to 81.12 points, 2.72 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
